course_name_en: Refrigeration, Air Conditioning and Heat Pump Technology 2
prerequisites: Basic knowledge from Thermodynamics and Fluid Mechanics given by MABB310 and MABB410, in particular: understanding of basic thermodynamic and fluid mechanics principles and laws, basics of heat transfer.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to thoroughly assess the energetic and ecological significance of air conditioning systems and heat pumps with concrete reference to their use in buildings.
Students are able to apply meteorological and thermo-physiological principles to the planning and analysis of building energy technology systems.
Students can name influencing factors of thermal comfort, evaluate them using PMV and PPD indices, and mathematically record central air treatment processes and represent them in suitable diagrams.
Students are capable of calculating cooling loads, heating loads, and air volume flows for the design of building technical systems.
Students design, calculate, and analyze processes and systems in this context.
Students independently solve specific problems and critically question the application and significance of the technologies.

syllabus_topics: Basic structure of building energy technology systems
Building classification by typology (residential, non-residential, special buildings)
Structure of building energy technology based on the three-part division of supply concepts by generation, distribution, and delivery
Central and decentralized systems
Individual building supply vs. district heating supply
Renewable and conventional heat generators, especially heat pumps
Heat distribution (hydraulic networks and distribution systems, hydraulic circuits and basic fittings)
Heat emission (radiators, surface heating)
Integration of heat storage
Design of main components (heat generators, storage)
Evaluation and classification of the quality of energy supply concepts (system efficiency factors, CO2 emissions, COP, JAZ, SCOP, eta-S), legal requirements
Introduction to ventilation and air conditioning technology and knowledge of the most important components and systems of room air and air conditioning systems and plants
Meteorological basics: atmosphere, solar radiation, humidity, air temperature, wind
Physiological and technological requirements for air conditioning: thermal comfort, cooling load, heating demand

Thermodynamics of air treatment: characteristic values and state changes of moist air, Mollier h,X diagram: heating, cooling and dehumidifying, humidifying with liquid water and steam, pressure increase with fans, humidifying and dehumidifying with sorption
Design of air conditioning systems: cooling load, heating load calculation, outside air volume flow, supply air volume flow
Air conditioning units and central systems: structure of air conditioning units and central systems, fans, heat exchangers, humidifiers and dehumidifiers, air filters, air ducts
Air flows in air-conditioned rooms: chilled ceilings; basics, forms and types of air outlets, design examples (e.g. residential ventilation).
Measurement and control in air conditioning technology: measurement of air velocities, temperatures, humidity, air volume flows; control of air conditioning systems and their components
Heat recovery in air conditioning technology: regenerators, recuperators

assessment_methods.method: Study achievement: Lab reports in MABB642D
